about.title: El Segundo Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: El Segundo is a small city, but it packs a lot of pedestrian activity into its downtown core, its shopping centers off Sepulveda Boulevard, and the office and hotel properties near the coast. Uneven pavement, spilled liquids, loose mats, or a broken handrail can turn an ordinary errand into a serious injury. California law doesn't automatically make a property owner responsible just because someone got hurt on their land — you generally have to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn people about it. That's why what happens right after a fall matters: photos of the hazard, incident reports, and store or building surveillance footage can all disappear or get overwritten quickly. Our team listens to what happened and can start gathering evidence and dealing with the property owner or their insurer while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Evidence and Timing Matter in a California Premises Case

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: Under California law, you generally need to show the property owner or manager knew about the hazard, or should have discovered it through reasonable inspection, before it hurt you. We can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish that knowledge.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Last
items.desc: Many stores, offices, and hotels overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a formal preservation request out quickly is often the difference between having proof of the hazard and having nothing. Our team can handle that for you.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so even if you're found partly responsible for not seeing the hazard, you can still recover a share of damages proportional to the property owner's fault. We can help push back on inflated fault arguments from an insurer.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in El Segundo?
items.answer: In most cases against a private property owner, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned or managed by a government entity — for example, a municipal building or a public sidewalk maintained by the city — that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just months, so it's worth getting advice quickly.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near Sepulveda or Pacific Coast Highway and no one wrote up a report?
items.answer: A missing incident report isn't the end of your options. Photos of the hazard, witness statements, and your own notes about the conditions can still support a claim, and we can request the store or restaurant's internal records and any camera footage separately.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact you?
items.answer: No. Our team is here to help at no cost to you. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
